root_cause.text: The bcmasp WoL IRQ cleanup path incorrectly treated a devm-managed IRQ requested with devm_request_irq() as manually managed and called free_irq() on priv->wol_irq during probe error and remove, causing a double free.
root_cause.evidence: The patch deletes bcmasp_wol_irq_destroy(), which did `free_irq(priv->wol_irq, priv)`, and removes its calls from `bcmasp_probe()` error handling and `bcmasp_remove()`, while the commit message explicitly states “We do not need to free wol_irq since it was instantiated with devm_request_irq(). So devres will free for us.”

So devres will free for us.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the unused or redundant bcmasp_wol_irq_destroy helper that wrapped conditional free_irq cleanup.
intent_record.what: A static helper function named bcmasp_wol_irq_destroy was removed entirely; the deleted function checked whether priv->wol_irq was greater than 0 and, if so, called free_irq(priv->wol_irq, priv).
intent_record.how: This change eliminates that wrapper function from the codebase, so any cleanup of the Wake-on-LAN IRQ must now be handled elsewhere or the function was unused; by itself, the shown hunk does not introduce new runtime behavior beyond removing this local abstraction.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove WoL IRQ destruction from bcmasp_probe() error cleanup to avoid incorrect cleanup on probe failure.
intent_record.what: The call to bcmasp_wol_irq_destroy(priv) was removed from the err_cleanup label in bcmasp_probe(), leaving only bcmasp_remove_intfs(priv) before returning ret.
intent_record.how: On the probe error cleanup path, Wake-on-LAN IRQ destruction is no longer performed at this label, which avoids tearing down that IRQ resource in this specific cleanup sequence and changes cleanup responsibility to another path or prevents an invalid/double destroy during probe failure.

intent_record.intent_summary: Stop destroying the WoL IRQ during bcmasp_remove() to avoid incorrect or redundant teardown in the driver removal path.
intent_record.what: The call to bcmasp_wol_irq_destroy(priv); was removed from bcmasp_remove(struct platform_device *pdev), leaving only the null check on priv and the subsequent call to bcmasp_remove_intfs(priv).
intent_record.how: At runtime, the driver removal path no longer explicitly destroys the Wake-on-LAN IRQ in bcmasp_remove(). This changes teardown behavior so that IRQ cleanup is no longer performed at this point, likely avoiding duplicate or incorrect cleanup if it is handled elsewhere.

relevance_review.reason: The removed helper specifically wrapped conditional free_irq() cleanup for the WoL IRQ, which is the incorrect manual cleanup at the heart of the double-free root cause for a devm-managed IRQ.
The changes directly remove manual WoL IRQ cleanup in probe error and remove paths, matching the root cause that a devm-managed IRQ was incorrectly freed with free_irq(), causing double free.

candidates.rationale: This is the direct incorrect cleanup operation: it manually frees a WoL IRQ that was requested with devm_request_irq(), leading to a double free when devres later releases it.
This probe error path invokes the buggy helper, causing manual IRQ teardown for a devm-managed IRQ during probe failure cleanup.
This remove path invokes the buggy helper, incorrectly freeing a devm-managed IRQ during device removal and causing redundant teardown/double free.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the root incorrect operation: it manually frees priv->wol_irq even though the IRQ was allocated with devm_request_irq(), so devres will also free it later, resulting in a double free.

This statement is vulnerable because it invokes the buggy cleanup helper from the probe error path, which in turn calls free_irq() on a devm-managed IRQ and triggers the double-free condition during probe cleanup.

This statement is vulnerable because it invokes the buggy cleanup helper from the remove path, causing manual teardown of a devm-managed WoL IRQ and leading to redundant cleanup/double free on device removal.

diff --git a/drivers/net/ethernet/broadcom/asp2/bcmasp.c b/drivers/net/ethernet/broadcom/asp2/bcmasp.c
index 834
bic_trace_step.reason: The diff is sufficient because it shows both the IRQ allocation and cleanup logic. In `bcmasp_get_and_request_irq()`, the WoL IRQ is obtained and registered with `devm_request_irq(&pdev->dev, irq, bcmasp_isr_wol, 0, pdev->name, priv);`, which makes the IRQ devm-managed. However, the same commit adds explicit manual cleanup functions: `bcmasp_wol_irq_destroy_shared()` does `if (priv->wol_irq > 0) free_irq(priv->wol_irq, priv);` and `bcmasp_wol_irq_destroy_per_intf()` iterates interfaces and does `if (intf->wol_irq > 0) free_irq(intf->wol_irq, priv);`. Those destroy hooks are then called on probe failure (`priv->destroy_wol(priv);` before `bcmasp_remove_intfs(priv);`) and on remove (`priv->destroy_wol(priv);`). This is exactly the vulnerable construct described: a devm-managed IRQ requested with `devm_request_irq()` is also freed manually with `free_irq()`, creating a double-free/invalid cleanup path. No fix is present in this commit; the incorrect manual `free_irq()` paths remain.
